class.name: CameraRig3D
class.brief_description: A 3D camera rig that follows a target and supports first-person and third-person camera control.
class.description: CameraRig3D is a camera controller that manages a [Camera3D] node to provide target following, position smoothing, automatic look-at behavior, and optional mouse controls. The rig can create its own Camera3D child or adopt an existing Camera3D in its hierarchy, depending on [member adopt_existing_camera]. The managed camera is made current when the rig is initialized. The [member target] property specifies the [Node3D] that the rig follows. The [member follow_offset] property defines the desired position relative to the target. When position smoothing is enabled, the rig moves towards this position gradually instead of snapping to it. The [member camera_mode] property selects between [constant THIRD_PERSON] and [constant FIRST_PERSON], as defined by [enum CameraMode]. In third-person mode, captured mouse movement rotates the follow offset around the target, and the camera can automatically look at the target. In first-person mode, horizontal mouse movement rotates the target, while vertical mouse movement controls the camera's pitch. The [member mouse_orbit_enabled] property enables mouse controls. The [member mouse_orbit_sensitivity], [member mouse_orbit_pitch_min], and [member mouse_orbit_pitch_max] properties control mouse sensitivity and vertical rotation limits. The [method get_mouse_orbit_yaw] method returns the horizontal orbit angle used by third-person mode, which can be used for camera-relative movement. CameraRig3D can be used for third-person cameras and first-person setups. Nodes such as [SpringArm3D] can be used to handle camera collision in third-person mode.

method.name: get_mouse_orbit_yaw
method.description: Returns the current horizontal mouse orbit angle in radians. This can be used to make character movement relative to the camera's horizontal orientation in third-person mode.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the rig searches for an existing [Camera3D] in its hierarchy instead of creating a new camera. Cameras inside nested viewports are ignored.
The camera control mode. See [enum CameraMode].

The desired position offset from the target, expressed in the target's local space. The offset is transformed by the target's global transform. In third-person mode with mouse orbit enabled, the offset's Z component determines the orbit distance, while its X and Y components remain positional offsets.
If [code]true[/code], the rig follows the target using [member follow_offset].
If [code]true[/code], the managed camera points towards the target in third-person mode.

If [code]true[/code], captured mouse movement controls the camera. In third-person mode, it rotates the follow offset. In first-person mode, it rotates the target horizontally and the camera vertically. Mouse input is ignored while the mouse is not captured.
The maximum vertical mouse rotation angle in radians.
The minimum vertical mouse rotation angle in radians.
Scales mouse movement when calculating horizontal and vertical rotation. Higher values make the camera controls more sensitive.

If [code]true[/code], the rig smoothly interpolates towards its desired position after initialization. Otherwise, it moves directly to the desired position. First-person mode updates the follow position directly. [b]Note:[/b] During initialization, the rig is placed directly at the desired position.
Controls how quickly the rig approaches its desired position when [member position_smoothing_enabled] is enabled. Higher values make the camera follow more quickly.
The [Node3D] that the rig follows and, in third-person mode, looks at. If no target is assigned, target-dependent updates are not performed. Changing the target resets the mouse orbit angles.

constants.constant: The camera orbits around the target and can look towards it.
The target controls horizontal rotation, while the camera controls vertical rotation.
